title: The forty as a life
hook: intention, the pillars, the heart, the tongue, mercy: al-Nawawi's forty, read first to last, run like one life
tomorrow: you've read all forty. could you say even one without your phone?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last of the forty-two: as long as you call, the door stays open, even for sins reaching the clouds. Today, all of them at once.
screen: `AS LONG AS YOU CALL.` → `ALL OF THEM AT ONCE.`

segments.voice: The lights go down in the gym and the senior slideshow starts. A toddler in a birthday crown, a missing front tooth, a science fair volcano, a prom photo. Nobody in the room sees a stack of pictures. They see one life, in order. Now run al-Nawawi's forty-two hadith like that slideshow, first to last. It opens on intention. It closes on a voice saying: as long as you call. So what happens in between, and why does a book of foundations end on someone who has failed?
screen: `THE SENIOR SLIDESHOW.` → `ONE LIFE, IN ORDER.` → `WHY END ON FAILING?`

segments.voice: Watch the order. Frame one: actions are by intentions. Before anything, why. Then a stranger in white sits knee to knee with the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and lays out the map of the religion, ending with worship Allah as if you see Him. Then the pillars, the frame of the house. Then the inside: a lump of flesh in the body that, when it's sound, keeps the whole body sound. The heart. Then the tongue: speak good or be silent. Then other people, everywhere: love for your brother what you love for yourself, relieve a distress, no harm. Near the end, a traveler: be in the world as a stranger, or someone passing through. And the last frame isn't a trophy. It's a sacred hadith in Tirmidhi's collection, in paraphrase: as long as you call on Me and hope in Me, I forgive you, and I don't mind. That's the answer. A life built on the first forty-one still slips, so the book leaves the door open. Al-Nawawi never says he arranged it as a life; that's one way to read his order. But here's a thing to tell a friend tonight: the collection that starts with why you do things ends with what to do when you didn't.
screen: `FIRST, THE WHY.` · `THE MAP, THE PILLARS, THE HEART.` · `THE TONGUE, THEN EVERYONE ELSE.` · `A DOOR LEFT OPEN.` · then, large: `A LIFE IN FORTY.`

segments.voice: On a scrap of paper, write by hand the three of the forty-two you'd keep if you could keep only three. Short names are fine: intention, the heart, as long as you call. For the sit, look at the three together and notice what kind of day they'd make.
screen: `THREE YOU'D KEEP.` · `WHAT DAY WOULD THEY MAKE?`

segments.voice: The forty as a life: al-Nawawi's hadith read first to last, intention at the start and a door left open at the end.
screen: `THE FORTY AS A LIFE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Hold onto this: a life in forty, the why at the start and the door still open at the end. Until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1471 COUNTS.` → `THE FORTY, GATHERED · 1 OF 3 · YEAR FIVE, 45 OF 365.` → `TOMORROW: YOU'VE READ ALL FORTY. COULD YOU SAY EVEN ONE WITHOUT YOUR PHONE?`

howItsDone: Muslims who study al-Nawawi's forty often go back over the whole set when they finish, choosing a few to keep close; teachers commonly review it from the first hadith to the last.

match.prompt: the forty, first to last — tap the pairs.

myth: the forty end on a reward list for the best believers
the last hadith is about someone who has failed and calls; the door stays open.

fork.setup: you finished all forty-two and feel like a fraud: you know them, and you still snapped at your sister today. what does the last hadith say?
options: close the book; knowing them without living them is pointless.
the collection ends on calling and being forgiven; come back and keep going.
intention is what counts, so the snapping doesn't really matter.
fork.reveal: the book of foundations ends with a door left open: as long as you call on Me and hope in Me, I forgive you.

original.note: Arabic: forty. the collection is known as al-Arba'in, the forty, though it holds forty-two.

trapdoor: what you thought: forty-two separate sayings to memorize.
what it means: read in order, they run like a life: the why, the map, the heart, the tongue, other people, and a door left open.
what a scholar hears: al-Nawawi chose each as a foundation; reading the order as a life is a reading, not his stated plan.
guess: al-Nawawi's hadith read in order, like one life
the forty days a new Muslim studies before praying
a rule to read one hadith a year for forty years

chat.meaning: The forty start with intention: actions are by intentions. Before the pros and cons comes the why.

al-Nawawi.meaning: a scholar from Syria who gathered these forty-two hadith

hadith.meaning: a report of what the Prophet said or did

Tirmidhi.meaning: a scholar whose hadith collection records the last of the forty

sources.ref: al-Nawawi, al-Arba'in al-Nawawiyyah, hadith 1, 2, 3, 6, 13, 15, 32, 36, 40, 42 (intention; the stranger in white; built on five; the lump of flesh; love for your brother; speak good or be silent; no harm; relieve a distress; a stranger or a traveler; as long as you call)
